picks.name: Confetti Kick Pocket
picks.why: Top score (4.172), textbook feel (devSd .082, lag1 .559); hat alternates loud/soft each downbeat, kick stays ghosted so beat 1 breathes.

picks.name: Eighth-Note Roller
picks.why: Kick actually lands on 1 and syncopations (not just ghosts), snare ghosts flank the backbeat for real dynamic architecture.

picks.name: Phantom Pulse
picks.why: Highest lag1 in the bucket (.713), kick fully ghosted, one hat accent per bar — most spacious felt-not-heard pocket, good contrast pick.

picks.name: Fast Train Beat
picks.why: Only fast-tempo pick (148bpm), quarter-note snare drive; bar 2 drops one kick hit to a ghost so halves relate but aren't identical.

picks.name: One-Drop Lift
picks.why: Kick only on downbeats leaves space, hat carries ghost/accent detail, single open hihat before the loop point gives a clean turnaround.

picks.name: Classic Backbeat
picks.why: Real kick pulse under a clean backbeat snare and alternating X/x/◦ hat; solid feel stats (devSd .081, lag1 .529).

picks.name: Sixteenth Wash
picks.why: Near-every-16th hat wash is a unique texture here, fuller kick than its ghost-kick cousins; same tempo as #0 but a different gesture entirely.

picks.name: Half-Time Ride
picks.why: Only ride/crash/tom-led pick instead of hat-lead; sparse kick/snare under a loping ride adds real instrumentation diversity, lag1 .54.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if the brief needs a hard devSd 0.02-0.10/lag1>0.2 filter (cuts #4, #38), or if two 86bpm entries count against tempo diversity despite differing kick/hat design.

picks.name: Slow Ghost Pocket
picks.why: Top score in the bucket; ghost-laden hat builds real velocity waves around a textbook 2/4 backbeat with a breathing beat one.

picks.name: Crash Cue Funk
picks.why: Crash cue on one plus open-hat lifts give it a produced, song-start feel without losing the syncopated kick pocket.

picks.name: Latin Sixteenth Skip
picks.why: Evenly alternating hat over a Latin-tinged kick skip, tight sweet-spot devSd/lag1 for the smoothest loop of its family.

picks.name: Busy Hand Groove
picks.why: Only take from a second drummer in the bucket — denser, more syncopated hand than everything else here.

picks.name: Fast Ride Shuffle
picks.why: Ride-carried shuffle at the bucket's fastest tempo; kick stays sparse and open while the ride swings hard.

picks.name: Snare Pop Space
picks.why: Signature double snare pop near beat two with the kick almost absent, leaving a huge, distinct pocket.

picks.name: Breathing Beat One
picks.why: Kick lands as a ghost on beat one instead of an accent, giving the most literal 'beat one breathing' pocket in the set.

picks.name: Evolving Latin Turn
picks.why: Bar two trades hat-drive for snare/crash/open accents — a real two-bar arc rather than a copy-pasted loop.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Audition shows #17/#22's sparse or evolving kick reads as broken pocket, not intentional space, or #18 sounds too close to another drummer7 grid.

picks.name: Breathing Pocket
picks.why: Clean 4-way backbeat with a syncopated kick that leaves beat 1 open and a hat line built from real ghost-to-accent dynamics.

picks.name: Slow Roll Boom Bap
picks.why: Laid-back 75bpm dotted-eighth kick under a swung hat; the last backbeat rushes in on a ghost-note buildup for forward pull.

picks.name: Rimshot Bounce
picks.why: Bar1's beat-2 backbeat lands as a rimshot instead of snare, a genuine human substitution that keeps the loop from feeling stamped.

picks.name: Ghost Kick Shuffle
picks.why: Slowest tempo in the bucket, an entirely ghost-voiced kick under a dense swung hat -- the deepest ghost architecture (29 ghosts) here.

picks.name: Fade Out Fill
picks.why: Kick thins out then rebuilds into an accented fill right at the loop point while the hat drops out early, giving the bars real shape.

picks.name: Syncopated Wave
picks.why: Front-accented syncopated kick with ghost grace notes and a hat that swells from ghost to accent -- the best human-timing fit in the set.

picks.name: Four Corner Kick
picks.why: Kick anchors beats 1 and 3 with a syncopated fill breaking up the second half, paired with a harder-hitting, less ghost-heavy hat for contrast.

picks.name: Halftime Sizzle
picks.why: Fastest tempo here, snare pulled off the standard backbeat into a half-time cluster, with tom/perc coloring giving the loop a verse-into-turnaround arc.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If devSd>0.10 must hard-disqualify despite strong lag1 (rules out #0, #6, #30), or if one-pick-per-drummer is required, favoring drummer5's flatter, backbeat-light #35 over musical strength.

picks.name: Ghost-Kick Pocket
picks.why: All-ghost kick leaves beat 1 open, clean 2&4 snare, 3-tier hat wave; devSd .090/lag1 .606 sit in the correlated sweet spot.

picks.name: Straight-Eighth Roll
picks.why: Syncopated ghost kick under a straight-8th hat, highest humanness (vr .961) of the bucket, tempo no other pick covers; devSd .094 ideal.

picks.name: Soft Build Crescendo
picks.why: Kick, pedal-hat and ride step ghost-to-mid bar1→bar2 together, a real architected wave; devSd .085/lag1 .207 in the preferred band.

picks.name: Tom Fill Pickup
picks.why: Bar-1-only tom fill makes halves related-not-identical for a clean loop, plus a soft-to-accent snare flam; lag1 .366, devSd .098.

picks.name: Kick Turnaround
picks.why: Different player from the groove7 cluster, clean 2&4 backbeat, extra kick hit closing bar 2 into a real turnaround.

picks.name: Ghost Note Wash
picks.why: Highest ghost count in the bucket (17), a third drummer, and a rare hat silence gap; lag1 .32 confirms felt, not random.

picks.name: Half-Time Flourish
picks.why: Only half-time-feel phrase (backbeat lands on 3), snare flourish closing bar 2 into the loop; covers the top tempo slot.

picks.name: Crash Intro Build
picks.why: Crash open, steady ride 8ths, backbeat itself grows soft-to-full across the phrase: a snare-driven dynamic arc, distinct from #7/#16.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if the 142bpm snare-on-3 is a tracking glitch not a half-time feel (kills #20), or if raw score should override my devSd/lag1 weighting, favoring near-dupes #0/#1/#3 instead.

picks.name: Quarter Pulse Rock
picks.why: Kick on 1/3 with clean ghost transitions, steady quarter hat, rock-solid backbeat; top score in bucket, best lag1 (.79) of any straight-rock candidate.

picks.name: Ghost Kick Sway
picks.why: Kick fully ghosted, driving 16th hat carries momentum, clean backbeat; devSd .093/lag1 .71 nail correlated-feel at a rare slow 60bpm tempo.

picks.name: Linear Snare Weave
picks.why: Snare-led linear pattern, kick reduced to texture, tom/ride fills; busiest dynamic architecture in the set, a real break from four-on-floor rock.

picks.name: Ride-Driven Backbeat
picks.why: Ride cymbal, not hat, carries time over syncopated kick and ghost-dense snare; different drummer, clean stats (devSd .098/lag1 .585).

picks.name: Polyrhythmic Pocket
picks.why: Layered tom/ride/pedal ostinato under a linear 16th kick; best lag1 (.785) of any complex pattern here, from a third distinct drummer.

picks.name: Bell Pocket Groove
picks.why: No hi-hat at all; pedal chick and bell carry time while kick/snare accents step down bar to bar. Cleanest stats in the bucket (devSd .079, lag1 .832).

picks.name: Rock Shuffle Swing
picks.why: Only genuine swing/shuffle feel in the bucket — triplet ride and swung ghost snare over steady soft kick; devSd .096 in the human-feel range.

picks.name: Bell Ghost Backbeat
picks.why: Simple quarter-note kick anchor against a dense ghost/accent snare wave plus bell hits; a fourth distinct drummer, unlike anything else picked.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Strict devSd<=0.10 as a hard cutoff would bump #0/#2/#26 (devSd .11-.14); a brief wanting only straight high-energy rock would drop #8/#2/#38 as off-genre.

picks.name: Snare Ramp to Toms
picks.why: Snare crescendo through beat 3 spills straight into a full last-beat tom run, landing hard on one.

picks.name: Second-Line Simmer
picks.why: Ghost kicks and syncopated toms simmer across the whole bar before one snare stab caps it.

picks.name: Shuffle Crescendo
picks.why: Ghost-to-accent snare crescendo hands off cleanly to a short tom run and floor punch.

picks.name: Space Then Toms
picks.why: Opens with ghost snare, drops to silence, then a quick tom run lands on one kick right at the edge.

picks.name: Hats Out Snare In
picks.why: Hi-hats thin out as the snare builds through beat two, toms cap the last beat.

picks.name: Full Bar Crescendo
picks.why: Snare and floor tom climb together across the entire bar into a hard accent right on the line.

picks.name: Boom Bap Runup
picks.why: Snare pops, a beat of space, then a tom crescendo lands on a single kick right before one.

picks.name: Halftime Tom Pulse
picks.why: An unbroken eighth-note tom pulse rides the whole bar, easing to a lone kick before the downbeat.

picks.name: Slow Build Sprint
picks.why: A patient snare-and-floor build gives way to an accelerating tom run right at the bar's edge.

picks.name: Backporch Triplets
picks.why: Busy snare work up front clears out for a clean triplet tom run into the next bar.

picks.name: Snare Cluster Slam
picks.why: A quick floor-tom stab up front, then a tight snare cluster detonates right on the bar line.

picks.name: Open Hat Tom Dive
picks.why: Open hi-hats give way to a building snare, then toms take over the entire last beat.

picks.name: Crash and Breathe
picks.why: Snare and floor tom activity builds to a crash on beat four, then lets the space ring into one.

picks.name: Late Floor Rally
picks.why: Early snare-and-kick action clears out for a three-hit floor tom rally landing at the bar's edge.

picks.name: Snare Stack Landing
picks.why: A steady kick anchors a snare crescendo that stacks into toms and a floor-tom landing.

picks.name: Reggae Tom Skank
picks.why: Alternating toms pulse through the back half of the bar in a hypnotic offbeat turn.

picks.name: Ghost Snare Whisper
picks.why: A single snare lane of ghosts and accents that quietly tightens into two accents right at the line.

picks.name: Rhumba Ghost Rise
picks.why: Quiet ghost notes rise into a snare crescendo that lands just before the downbeat.

picks.name: Quiet Into the Storm
picks.why: A hushed opening erupts into a dense floor-tom storm that stays hot clear to the bar line.

picks.name: Long Snare Roll Out
picks.why: Open hats and kick set up a huge snare roll that fills the entire second half of the bar.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Audio reveals the ASCII arc doesn't translate sonically (e.g. #33/#14/#37 sit buried, or rejected busy-groove baiao/repetitive fills actually swing as felt fills).

picks.name: Breath Pocket Funk
picks.why: Top score in the bucket; syncopated ghost-note kick leaves beat one open while snare/hat build a real velocity wave (vr .945).

picks.name: Tresillo Bomba Pulse
picks.why: Classic NOLA bomba kick with spang-a-lang pedal foundation; strong lag1 (.485) matches the genre's rolling triplet phrasing.

picks.name: Rudimental Snare Roll
picks.why: Snare carries the phrase in a ghost/accent roll over a steady quarter kick -- a different secondline construction than the bomba pick.

picks.name: Chacha Crescendo Build
picks.why: Snare ghosts bloom into a hard accent at the loop seam, giving the widest dynamic range (vr .906) of the chacha material.

picks.name: Chacha Steady Bed
picks.why: Cross-stick/hat carry an understated pulse with the best-calibrated feel stats in the bucket (lag1 .243, devSd .110); a bed under the crescendo pick.

picks.name: Accented Funk Drive
picks.why: Different drummer/tempo from the ghost-kick pick; accented downbeat kick, busy open-hat, clean loop with a subtle tail lift into the repeat.

picks.name: Funk Turnaround Fill
picks.why: Shares the driving pocket of pick 10 but stacks a kick flourish across bar two (lag1 .307) -- a turnaround companion, not a duplicate loop.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if the score already outweighs my grid reading -- e.g. #1 (best lag1, .281) should replace #0, or #15 is a near-dupe of #10 and the set should shrink to 6.

picks.name: Sixteenth Drive
picks.why: Densest syncopated 16th kick against a 14-ghost hat wave — highest score in the bucket, backbone disco pocket.

picks.name: Ghost Wave Pocket
picks.why: Sparsest kick leaves beat 1 open; 18 ghosts on the hat at the tightest devSd (0.096) in the whole set — most controlled human feel.

picks.name: Open Hat Shuffle
picks.why: Classic accented four-on-floor with a busy shuffled hat and one open-hat accent for lift — a clean, useful workhorse groove.

picks.name: Ghost Snare Groove
picks.why: Snare carries the dynamic wave (21 ghosts, most in the set) over an unaccented kick — a genuinely different architecture from the hat-led picks.

picks.name: Crash Turnaround
picks.why: Toms and crash build into a turnaround fill over a steady four-on-floor pulse, giving the loop a real release point instead of flat repetition.

picks.name: Cowbell Pulse
picks.why: Ride-and-bell disco groove, sparse and iconic, gives real breathing room against the busier hat-driven picks.

picks.name: Ride Escalation
picks.why: Ride pattern escalates into triplet accents across bar two — an actual crescendo arc, not a flat loop, at near-ideal devSd (0.103).

picks.name: Hat Syncopation
picks.why: Hat-driven breakbeat syncopation with the best lag1 (0.517) of the 170bpm tracks, signaling genuinely correlated human timing.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If ghost/accent symbols don't map to real audible dynamics, or picks 2/6/7/11 (all disco-120 four-on-floor) sound too similar despite differing snare/hat/cymbal layers.

picks.name: Breathing Downbeat
picks.why: Kick lands soft (x, not X) on beat 1 then bites hard through the bar; devSd .093/lag1 .50 sit right in the human-feel target zone.

picks.name: Bell Cascade Bloom
picks.why: Bell, rim, tambourine, kick and snare each carry their own ghost/accent line simultaneously — the richest dynamic architecture in the whole bucket.

picks.name: Ghost Decay Groove
picks.why: Kick ghosts thin out from bar 1 into bar 2 while snare answers with a matching wave — halves relate without repeating, clean arc into the loop point.

picks.name: Call And Response
picks.why: Bar 1 argues entirely on hat, bar 2 answers entirely on toms — a genuine trade figure, and the highest dynamic-variance score (vr .96) in the set.

picks.name: Silent One Shuffle
picks.why: Kick nearly vanishes so beat 1 breathes wide open; rimshot cascade carries the pulse and tapers into the turnaround — very loopable arc.

picks.name: Hat Weave Ostinato
picks.why: Dense 16th-note hat with real X/x accent shading over a whisper-quiet kick — a different functional role than every kick-driven pick, devSd .082/lag1 .41 clean.

picks.name: Afro Bell Sway
picks.why: Bell carries the ostinato while the kick lives entirely in off-beat ghosts — the only bell-forward texture picked, strong lag1 .48.

picks.name: Tom Cross Bounce
picks.why: Tom-and-snare cross-rhythm laid over a steady, softly-hit quarter-note kick — the bounce family's cleanest cross-stick ghost architecture.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if genre words count as banned source names, or if raw score-rank should override my de-duplication of near-identical drummer8/drummer5 grid clusters.

picks.name: Hat Groove Turn
picks.why: Top score in the bucket; steady hat groove with a sidestick/tom/crash flourish that lifts into bar 2 without crowding beat 1.

picks.name: Running Hat Drive
picks.why: Near-continuous 16th hat ostinato under a pure ghost-only snare — a stripped engine layer, highest velocity-range (vr .96) of the set.

picks.name: Swung Hat Skeleton
picks.why: Loosest, most human-feeling hat pattern here (lag1 .69) with only two snare hits, leaving maximum air in the pocket.

picks.name: Bell & Pedal Rhumba
picks.why: Genuine bell+pedal rhumba skeleton with a ghost/accent snare wave; devSd .097 sits squarely in the human-feel range.

picks.name: Calypso Kick Build
picks.why: Full-kit calypso groove whose kick crescendos into the bar-2 turn; strongest correlated hand-feel (lag1 .69) plus busiest ghost architecture.

picks.name: Triplet Ride Surge
picks.why: Only phrase with a real two-half arrangement — a triplet ride burst owns bar 1 then drops out, so the loop breathes instead of repeating flatly.

picks.name: Syncopated Ride Pulse
picks.why: Busy 16th ride against a steadily accented kick pulse gives this calypso pick a distinct, tighter texture from the other two.

picks.name: Tom Burst Handoff
picks.why: Floor-tom call in bar 1 is answered by bell+ride in bar 2 — an evolving two-bar shape (lag1 .375), not a copy-paste repeat.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If devSd/lag1 mostly reflect quantization noise rather than real hand timing, or if #9's silent-vs-active tom imbalance between bars gives an audible seam once actually looped.

picks.name: Foursquare Skank
picks.why: Kick pins every quarter while an accented skank hat and ghost-laced snare build the strongest pocket and dynamic wave in the set.

picks.name: Classic One Drop
picks.why: Archetypal reggae one-drop (kick only on 2 and 4) leaves beat one to breathe, giving genre-signature spaciousness the set otherwise lacks.

picks.name: Rockers Crash Kit
picks.why: Fastest tempo here, full-kit rockers arrangement with crash and open-hat lifts, and the best lag1 (.37) for a genuinely human pocket.

picks.name: Tom Tag Rockers
picks.why: Same rockers foundation as its sibling but dressed with sidestick, open-hat lifts and a floor-tom tag on the turnaround for a distinct shape.

picks.name: Locked Groove Hat
picks.why: Best human-feel stats in the bucket (lag1 .52, devSd .09, both in-range) riding a dense syncopated hat -- the pocket reference of the group.

picks.name: Steppers Pulse
picks.why: Rare dense eighth-note steppers kick under a churning hat gives real rhythmic contrast against the one-drop and rockers picks.

picks.name: Hat Bloom Pickup
picks.why: Near-silent bar one blooms into a hat-and-kick groove in bar two, giving the widest velocity range (.96) for arrangement transitions.

picks.name: Ghost Click One Drop
picks.why: A slow one-drop variant thick with ghost hats and sidestick clicks, adding dynamic density diversity at the tempo extreme.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if identical kick foundations (2/3/4) should be de-duped over embellishment differences, or if #7's near-empty first bar disqualifies it and #5 should replace it despite weaker lag1.

picks.name: Ride Pocket Groove
picks.why: Top overall score; ride ostinato and ghost snare interlock while kick stays out of beat one's way.

picks.name: Spang-a-Lang Walk
picks.why: Kick reduced to a single ghost note, leaving pure spang-a-lang ride time for a soloist to float over.

picks.name: Swing Shuffle Lift
picks.why: Looser shuffle feel from a different hand than the walking-ride pick, with lifting hat accents on top.

picks.name: Fusion Hat Weave
picks.why: Highest lag1 in the bucket (0.77) -- hat accents and tom hits breathe like a player thinking ahead of the beat.

picks.name: Open Air Fusion
picks.why: Kick nearly vanishes; devSd/lag1 sit right in the ideal window and the two bars stay related but never repeat.

picks.name: Fusion Hat Engine
picks.why: A motorik, denser-kick counterpart to the airier fusion picks -- same family, clearly different density.

picks.name: Linear Crest Fill
picks.why: True linear voicing building into an open-hihat accent at the bar line -- a swell for transitions, not a loop-and-forget groove.

picks.name: Second-Line Snare
picks.why: The only snare-led backbeat in the set, with a genuine ghost-to-accent wave instead of hat/ride driving the time.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if uniform lag1/devSd stats across all 8 matter more than genre diversity: #8, #23, #19 sit outside the ideal band, kept over higher-stat but redundant funk/fusion siblings.

picks.name: Porch Backbeat
picks.why: Kick sits only on the downbeats leaving huge space, while a ghost-dense snare builds a real backbeat wave (X on 2 & 4) at 78bpm.

picks.name: Feather Kick
picks.why: Softest kick voicing in the set (ghosted, not hit) with devSd 0.092 - the most naturally human-timed phrase in the bucket.

picks.name: Crash Corner Fill
picks.why: Adds toms, crash and open hat for a busier turnaround texture, diversifying the library's density beyond plain backbeats.

picks.name: Train Beat Drive
picks.why: Best lag1 in the bucket (0.505) with a kick that shifts its ghost placement bar-to-bar - an authentically human driving train beat.

picks.name: Ghost Wave Train
picks.why: Highest ghost count in the bucket (15) carves a real velocity wave under an accented downbeat and single ride color-hit.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If #5's identical bars are actually a feature (clean loop seam) for this engine, or if #0/#1 read as too redundant and one should be swapped for #5.

picks.name: Quarter Kick Bloom
picks.why: Ghost kicks on the quarter in bar 1 bloom to mid-velocity in bar 2, syncopated snare and a bar-2 crash give it a real turnaround.

picks.name: Sidestick Shuffle
picks.why: Ghost-flecked kick under a dense 8th-note ride with sidestick accents threaded through both bars for a churning, off-kilter groove.

picks.name: Pickup Into Pocket
picks.why: A near-silent snare pickup bar detonates into a kick/hat/sidestick groove in bar 2 -- the strongest velocity correlation (lag1 0.49) of the three.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: The bucket held more unseen candidates beating these on the lag1/devSd sweet spot, or #2's empty kick bar1 is a dropout artifact rather than an intentional pickup, undermining its loopability.

picks.name: Turnaround Roll
picks.why: Syncopated ghost-accent groove with a mid-bar snare roll that turns the phrase around cleanly; strong lag1/devSd show real human timing.

picks.name: Tight Pocket Vamp
picks.why: Tight, repeating ghost-kick syncopation with closed 8th hats; highest ghost count and second-best score, a dependable pocket loop.

picks.name: Half-Time Buildup
picks.why: Half-time backbeat builds tension across two bars then releases into a snare fill on the turnaround; best lag1 correlation (0.58) here.

picks.name: Ride Half-Time
picks.why: Ride-driven half-time cousin to the backbeat-buildup pick, with a different kick placement and cymbal color for texture diversity.

picks.name: Fast Minimal Backbeat
picks.why: Minimal, steady 144bpm backbeat with quarter-note hats, a clean foursquare contrast to the busier syncopated picks.

picks.name: Tom Build Explosion
picks.why: Floor-tom quarter-note build empties out then detonates into a five-hit snare fill and closing tom, the most dramatic release in the set.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If #5's negative lag1 reflects genre-authentic straight phrasing rather than sloppiness, or the library needs 8 slots filled regardless, #2 (open-hat variant) or #7 (ride groove) would belong too.

picks.name: Downbeat Anchor
picks.why: Top score with the tightest human stats (devSd .092, lag1 .61); firm beat-1 kick and quarter-note backbeat, halves vary just enough to loop clean.

picks.name: Floating One
picks.why: Kick ducks beat 1 entirely so open-hat and ghost snare carry the pulse instead—same family as the anchor but a genuinely different pocket philosophy.

picks.name: Bell and Ride Drive
picks.why: Constant ride plus a single bell strike on one gives real horn-section drive; dense kick under a wide dynamic spread at a slower 85bpm.

picks.name: Open Hat Cascade
picks.why: Open hat, not the kick, carries the pulse; kick becomes a cross-rhythm ornament. Cleanest human feel in the bucket (devSd .076, lag1 .64).

picks.name: Syncopated Pocket
picks.why: Kick drops off-grid into syncopation while a ghost-dense hat fills the gaps; strong lag1 gives it a real laid-back breathing pocket.

picks.name: Cross Stick Weave
picks.why: The one pick from a different drummer entirely—sparse kick under a woven hat/cross-stick lattice, highest lag1 outside the anchor family.

picks.name: Building Backbeat
picks.why: Snare ghost density visibly swells from bar 1 into bar 2—a real dynamics arc, not a flat loop—while the backbeat stays locked.

picks.name: Pedal Clock Groove
picks.why: Constant quarter-note pedal hihat acts as the clock under a syncopated ride and cross-rhythm kick—a driving-lane choice unlike any other pick.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Playback shows the higher-devSd picks (#4,#23,#13,#34) sound sloppy not human-swung, or #5's beat-1-avoiding kick reads as weak rather than spacious.

picks.name: Swung Hat Pulse
picks.why: Hat alternates ghost/mid/accent in a real wave over a repeating kick; one late snare accent + open-hat ornament in bar 2 keeps halves related, not identical.

picks.name: Roll To The One
picks.why: Hat drops out in bar 2 for a building ghost roll through kick/toms into a snare+floor accent that snaps back to beat one — a real fill, not a groove repeat.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If glyphs don't map cleanly to ghost/mid/accent velocity, or the library needs exactly 3/bucket, excluding #2 (score 3.064, vr 0.606, zero accents in any lane, flat dynamics) would be wrong.

picks.name: Open-Hat Pulse
picks.why: Kick every beat with one opening accent, dense sidestick ghosts beneath, open-hat swells bookend the bars; best pocket stats (lag1 .70).

picks.name: Tail-Accent Ride
picks.why: Ride ostinato carries time; kick accent lands late (4&) not on 1; one-shot bell/tom color gives the loop forward lean.

picks.name: Sidestick Weave
picks.why: Near-continuous sidestick ghost lattice over a deliberately flat, unaccented kick — pure textural bed, distinct from the accented-kick picks.

picks.name: Ride-Snare Duet
picks.why: Stripped to ride/snare/kick/pedal; ride and snare trade heavy accents in real call-and-response — sparsest, most percussively active pick.

picks.name: Tom-Fill Drive
picks.why: Fullest kit (kick/snare/ride/pedal/toms), accented kick every beat, late tom hit cueing a fill into the next phrase.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if #5 (dropped) is needed as a distinct fill/roll-out variant from #4 despite near-identical K/P lanes, or if devSd should outrank lag1, favoring #2 over #0 as top pick.

picks.name: Quiet Stairstep
picks.why: Clean 5-note stepwise fall (27→24→20→15→12) that lands squarely on the octave, no wobble.

picks.name: Home Turn
picks.why: Rises then mirrors back down to its own starting pitch — a tidy turn-figure ornament, not a noodle.

picks.name: Diving Swoop
picks.why: Gentle descent tips into one dramatic octave-plus dive and settles on the stable fifth — a real Nic-Nac gesture.

picks.name: Even Glide
picks.why: Five notes, even spacing, unbroken downward line — the simplest clean descending gesture in the set.

picks.name: Thirds Cascade
picks.why: Fast descending run in thirds (double-stops), under a beat long, lands cleanly — adds texture variety.

picks.name: Full Cascade
picks.why: Full 7-note scalar fall from the 12th down to the octave with zero direction changes — the purest long descent here.

picks.name: Skip to Rest
picks.why: Descends, hops up a third, then drops and holds the octave — a little cadential bounce before it settles.

picks.name: Lilting Drop
picks.why: Same descending shape but with rhythmic gaps between notes, giving it a lilting, dotted feel; lands on the octave.

picks.name: Flutter Fall
picks.why: Opens with a double-stop flutter and neighbor tone, then two long sustained notes fall to a rock-stable landing.

picks.name: Fourths Drop
picks.why: Unusual cascade descending in near-parallel fourths — a distinct color that stands apart from the stepwise runs.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If 'step' means real elapsed time not event order, some picks could span more than 2.5 beats; or if 'degree' isn't semitones-from-tonic, my stable-landing calls are wrong.

picks.name: Straight Drop Home
picks.why: Five-note accelerating descent (19-16-12-7-0) lands squarely on the tonic — the cleanest possible resolution.

picks.name: Long Fall Octave
picks.why: Smooth six-note stepwise fall spanning over an octave, settling cleanly on the octave.

picks.name: Quick Octave Dip
picks.why: Short crisp descent to the octave in about one beat — compact, punchy, done in one breath.

picks.name: Cascade to Fifth
picks.why: Confident seven-note cascade with even downward motion, resolving on the stable fifth above.

picks.name: Tumble and Land
picks.why: Steady descending run that accelerates into a bigger final drop, landing held on the octave.

picks.name: Fall with a Curl
picks.why: Clean descent to the octave capped with a light turn ornament that settles right back on it.

picks.name: Settle to Tonic
picks.why: Sustained opening tone eases down through a tiny neighbor wobble to a held tonic landing.

picks.name: Hop then Glide Home
picks.why: A small upward lift before a graceful stepwise glide home to the tonic.

picks.name: Grace Hold Descend
picks.why: A whisper-light grace note into a held tone, then one soft descending step to the octave.

picks.name: Hold Fall Perch
picks.why: Sustained anchor tone cascades down through a light turn, settling held on the fifth.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Audio shows same-step doublets sound like clashing notes not grace flourishes, or landing stability should weigh sounding harmony over raw semitone distance from tonic.

picks.name: Rising Stairs
picks.why: Eight evenly-spaced notes climb straight to the tonic octave, textbook clean ascending flourish.

picks.name: Thirds Climb
picks.why: Consistent +3 semitone steps glide up to land squarely on the tonic, very composed.

picks.name: Octave Reach
picks.why: Monotonic six-note climb with natural voice-leading, resolves cleanly on the octave.

picks.name: Bright Ascent
picks.why: Fast smooth run landing on the major third, gives an open non-tonic resolution option.

picks.name: Breath and Climb
picks.why: Held notes punctuate the ascent, giving a phrase-like breathing shape before landing on the octave.

picks.name: Settle Up High
picks.why: Ascending run with sustained top notes, settles warmly onto the tonic octave.

picks.name: Quick Lift
picks.why: Short punchy five-note lift to the fifth, compact enough for a quick end-of-phrase flick.

picks.name: Uneven Climb
picks.why: Slightly irregular step sizes give this ascent more character while still landing on the tonic.

picks.name: Leap and Fall
picks.why: Big upward leap followed by a short cascading fall back to the tonic octave, one clear gestural arc.

picks.name: Big Reach Settle
picks.why: Dramatic register leap up then eases back down to land firmly on the tonic, distinct arc shape for variety.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If gesture length should sum each note's own duration rather than use lenQn, several picks (#35, #17, #4) actually span 6-8 beats, too long for a sparse ornament.

picks.name: Coiled Leap
picks.why: Brief downward coil then a near two-octave leap settling on the 5th; compact spring-load shape.

picks.name: Rising Stair
picks.why: Five-note stepwise climb lands squarely on the tonic three octaves up; pure and direct.

picks.name: Leap and Release
picks.why: Sudden upward leap trickles back down to settle on the 5th, a classic sigh shape.

picks.name: Hold and Flick
picks.why: Long held note followed by a quick turn flourish landing on the tonic; maximally sparse.

picks.name: Mordent Rise
picks.why: Quick neighbor-tone dip kicks off a rising flourish that resolves cleanly on the octave.

picks.name: Turn to the Top
picks.why: Small oscillating turn launches a rising run that lands exactly on the tonic.

picks.name: Echo Step Rise
picks.why: Gentle ascending line with one repeated note before settling on the tonic; understated and clean.

picks.name: Quick Climb
picks.why: Six notes packed into a single beat race up to the tonic, the tightest fastest rise in the set.

picks.name: Turn and Reach
picks.why: A tidy neighbor-tone turn followed by one clean leap up to rest on the 5th.

picks.name: Turn and Land
picks.why: Same turn-then-leap gesture as its sibling but lands squarely on the tonic instead.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If audio shows duplicate-timestep notes (read as grace/turn dyads) sound as harsh clusters not quick ornaments, or lenQn isn't real seconds, some turn+leap picks could feel cluttered not sparse.

picks.name: Stairstep Echo
picks.why: Same turn shape restated a step lower, answering itself with a rest between and a quiet tail note.

picks.name: Twin Turn Whisper
picks.why: Two matching turn-figures separated by rest — a quiet call and its own answer.

picks.name: Sigh And Hold
picks.why: A two-note pickup into a long held tone, twice — reads like a breath between vocal lines.

picks.name: Tail Light Flicker
picks.why: Five quick steps tucked into the last beats after near-total silence — a closing wink, not a line.

picks.name: Late Drop To Rest
picks.why: Enters late, tumbles down in steps, and settles on the tonic — a clean landing after 22 steps of silence.

picks.name: Falling Half Answer
picks.why: A smooth stepwise descent that only speaks in the back half of the bar, leaving the front clear.

picks.name: Offbeat Nod
picks.why: A two-note nod that only ever lands off the beat, repeating a step lower each time it returns.

picks.name: Low Sway Answer
picks.why: Slow rock between two neighbor tones, always off the beat, sitting low and out of the vocal's way.

picks.name: Distant Ping
picks.why: Single tones dropped in every six steps — mostly air, a faint pulse rather than a competing line.

picks.name: Late Curl
picks.why: A tiny curling turn that only appears in the last beats, everything before it silent.

picks.name: Last Breath Run
picks.why: A quick seven-note stepwise slide packed into the final beats after nearly two bars of open rest.

picks.name: Overhead Descent
picks.why: A gentle stepwise fall two octaves above the vocal, always entering off the beat — never in the singer's way.

picks.name: Held Near Home
picks.why: Four long tones hovering a step or two from the tonic, all entering off the beat — pure held space.

picks.name: Quiet Downstep
picks.why: A calm four-step descent, every note entering off the beat, closing with a small turn.

picks.name: Rising Then Resting
picks.why: A short scalar climb that settles into two long held tones — an answer, then rest.

picks.name: Late Zigzag
picks.why: A brief up-down wobble near the end of the bar, mostly preceded by silence.

picks.name: Hold Then Flick
picks.why: One long tone fills most of the phrase, then a three-note flick right at the close.

picks.name: Opening Whisper
picks.why: A four-note fragment right at the top of the phrase, then nothing — leaves the rest of the bar open.

picks.name: Falling Into Hold
picks.why: A stepwise descent landing on a long held tone, every entrance placed off the beat.

picks.name: Middle Murmur
picks.why: A short three-step murmur in the middle of the bar, bookended by rest and a held close.

picks.name: Slow Fall Twice
picks.why: A short descending run into a long tone, echoed by a second held answer later in the phrase.

picks.name: Rising To Rest
picks.why: A clean stepwise climb from below the tonic up and back to rest, entering only after long silence.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: If 'clash' misses real friction vs the bass/chords, sparse drones (#46,#53) could clash more than shown; if the vocal sits low, low picks (#23,#47) need transposing up.

picks.name: Long Breath Answer
picks.why: Four long tones on offbeat entries with tiny stepwise motion back to tonic — pure space, no crowding.

picks.name: Call And Silence
picks.why: A 4-note whisper in bar one then total silence for bar two — hands the whole back half to the vocal.

picks.name: Second-Bar Nod
picks.why: Enters late, moves by a step or two, and leaves the rest of the phrase empty.

picks.name: Under-Breath Turn
picks.why: A quiet 3-note dip in bar one and a single echo note in bar two; never fills the room.

picks.name: Quiet Latecomer
picks.why: Sits entirely in bar two, narrow range, answers rather than announces.

picks.name: Tail-End Lift
picks.why: Small offbeat pulses near the phrase end with one gentle lift for a tag, not a hook.

picks.name: Steady Pulse Answer
picks.why: Evenly spaced single notes across both bars — a clock-tick answer that never crowds the beat.

picks.name: Mirror Sigh
picks.why: A tiny three-note arch stated twice, fully stepwise, sits in the back half of each bar.

picks.name: Fall And Rest
picks.why: Quick two-step fall into a long held tone, twice — breathes instead of competing.

picks.name: Offbeat Descent
picks.why: Three descending answer-pairs, every entrance offbeat, single clear downward contour.

picks.name: High Neighbor Tone
picks.why: Narrow neighbor-tone rock two octaves up — out of vocal range, high rest fraction.

picks.name: Closing Flicker
picks.why: A tiny turn only in the phrase's last quarter, otherwise silent — a closing flicker, not a line.

picks.name: Rise And Settle
picks.why: Confined arch shape in one window of the bar, single stepwise contour, resolves down.

picks.name: Rising Answer
picks.why: Clean single-direction rising scale confined to the second half of the phrase — one contour, singable.

picks.name: Dip Then Hold
picks.why: Small dip resolves into long sustained tones — mostly held space, minimal activity.

picks.name: Downward Sigh
picks.why: Smooth unbroken stepwise descent into a held note — one clear falling line.

picks.name: Overhead Descent
picks.why: Descending single-contour line perched high above the staff, entirely clear of a mid-register vocal.

picks.name: Settle And Glide
picks.why: Brief dip into a long hold, then a smooth stepwise glide down at the very end.

picks.name: Held Then Turn
picks.why: Two long held notes bookend a quick offbeat turn — mostly sustain, barely any motion.

picks.name: Narrow Sway
picks.why: Gentle stepwise sway in a narrow band, even pulses, easy to sing under or around.

picks.name: Overhead Shimmer
picks.why: Syncopated narrow oscillation two-plus octaves up — a shimmer that can't collide with a vocal.

picks.name: Drone And Flourish
picks.why: Long held drone note broken only by a brief triplet turn — nearly all space, minimal statement.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if rest/offbeat stats don't match perceived space once rendered (sustain masking silence), or if the lead vocal sits high, making register picks 23/43/57 clash.

picks.name: Undertow Walk
picks.why: Stepwise descent from near-root settles into a low sustained close, plenty of air for a vocal.

picks.name: High Perch Return
picks.why: Sustains a high octave anchor, then answers with a stepwise close back near the root.

picks.name: Stairway Rise
picks.why: Clean stepwise climb from near-root to a held octave, textbook walking-bass shape.

picks.name: Octave Heartbeat
picks.why: Alternates octave and leading tone squarely on the beat, a steady pulse with room to breathe.

picks.name: Low Held Sway
picks.why: Two long low holds then a gentle oscillation; ideal loop foundation under a voice.

picks.name: Descending Call
picks.why: Three falling calls land squarely on the root, sparse sustains give it a singable, spacious feel.

picks.name: Octave Cascade
picks.why: Full stepwise descent from the octave that resolves cleanly at the root.

picks.name: Rise To Root
picks.why: Stepwise climb from the low fifth straight to root, then a warm sustained tail.

picks.name: Root Swell
picks.why: Hovers on the root, arcs up through the octave, and settles — a clean tension-release shape.

picks.name: Rocking Third
picks.why: A tight repeating two-note rock that loops hypnotically without ever wandering off the pocket.

picks.name: Long Fall Home
picks.why: Enters late after silence and descends stepwise all the way to a held octave below.

picks.name: Groove Walk
picks.why: Genuine quarter-note walking line landing squarely on the octave — the most rhythm-section-ready of the set.

picks.name: Breath And Turn
picks.why: Mostly rest with a low octave anchor and one brief turn, resolving to root and octave.

picks.name: Deep Drop Settle
picks.why: A dramatic low leap resolves patiently back up through the octave to the fifth.

picks.name: Fifth Below Rock
picks.why: Sustained low fifths followed by a soft rocking figure near the root.

picks.name: Octave Ladder
picks.why: Low octave pedal with color tones, answered by a clean descending line from the octave above.

picks.name: Perfect Arch
picks.why: Fully stepwise rise-and-fall passing through the root — the most vocal-like contour in the bucket.

picks.name: Close Sway
picks.why: A tight rocking figure hugging the root with plenty of air around it, easy to loop.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if only pure sparse pedals count, or if the 2-notes/beat rule strictly bans the brief cushioned turns in #47 and #8.

picks.name: Rising Tonic Walk
picks.why: Eighth-note walk dips through the octave-below and climbs straight through the tonic to the sixth — a classic ascending walking bass.

picks.name: Low Call Homeward
picks.why: Low pedal opens into a descending turn figure that resolves to the tonic twice — a hooky, repeatable call-and-land riff.

picks.name: Stepwise Octave Fall
picks.why: 100% stepwise eighth-note descent through the tonic, landing dead on the octave below — the platonic walking bass.

picks.name: Octave to Home
picks.why: Opens on the octave, threads through the tonic mid-phrase, and lands squarely back on the tonic — constant, even eighths throughout.

picks.name: Fifth Call and Answer
picks.why: A held fifth above answered by a decorated fifth below — mirrored, stable, and made for looping under a vocal.

picks.name: Low Hum and Breath
picks.why: Under one note per beat with a long silence in the middle — pure space, ideal as a bed that never competes with a vocal.

picks.name: Octave Drop Walkdown
picks.why: Purposeful octave-to-octave leap opens a long, smooth stepwise descent that lands exactly on the tonic.

picks.name: Tonic Pedal Shimmer
picks.why: A grounded tonic pedal with breathing room gives way to a shimmering octave-register answer — grounded call, airy response.

picks.name: Octave Sway Descent
picks.why: Octave pedal with a gentle turn leads into an unhurried stepwise walk down — plenty of rest, easy to sit under a melody.

picks.name: Bare Octave Breath
picks.why: Only eight notes across two bars, resolving from the octave into a settled low fourth — maximum space, minimum flash.

picks.name: High Shimmer Settle
picks.why: Trilling figures pass through the octave and near-root before settling on a pedal fifth-below — the arpeggiated/shimmer texture the set needs.

picks.name: Octave Hold Tag
picks.why: A long octave-below pedal with most of the bar silent, capped by a light turn tag — very loop-friendly, lots of air.

picks.name: Home Three Times
picks.why: Returns to the tonic three separate times through a gentle dip-and-rise contour before lifting to an octave shimmer.

picks.name: Trill Pedal Turnaround
picks.why: A slow, hypnotic two-note pedal trill at quarter-note pace, capped with a quick ascending run as a turnaround into the loop.

picks.name: Octave Frame Turn
picks.why: Octave-below pedal bookends a tight, tuneful turn figure hovering right around the tonic — compact and endlessly loopable.

picks.name: Songful Dip and Rise
picks.why: Extremely smooth (92% stepwise, only 3 direction changes) arc from the tonic down and back, the most singable contour in the bucket.

picks.name: Walkdown to Octave
picks.why: Even eighth-note descent through the tonic that lands precisely on the octave below — textbook resolved walking line.

picks.name: Swung Fifth Descent
picks.why: Enters late after 3.5 beats of silence, then a smooth swung descent from the fifth through the tonic twice to a low landing.

r.wouldBeWrongIf: Wrong if the printed numbers are relative deltas, not absolute semitones-from-tonic, or if duration units aren't a 16th-note grid (both underlie my rootedness and busyness calls).
